gloss: drink; feast, banquet; (also) warp of a loom; buttocks
summary: To drink: water from a well, a stream or the rock, wine at a meal, and with אָכַל “eat” the whole of a shared meal, a feast, or a fast when neither is done. To plant a vineyard and drink its wine is the blessing of a settled people, and planting it and not drinking is the curse; to drink the cup from Yahweh's hand is to take his judgment, and Jesus spoke of the cup his Father gave him to drink. The noun מִשְׁתֶּה is the feast or banquet where men drink, and also what is drunk. Akkadian šatû, Ugaritic and Punic šty, Ge'ez sätyä and the Aramaic and Syriac verb all mean “drink”. The same letters also give שְׁתִי “warp” (Akkadian šutû, Arabic satan) and שֵׁת “buttocks” (Arabic ist), whose tie to drinking is not shown.

words.summary: About 216 times, almost all qal; the causative “give to drink” is another root, שָׁקָה. The brief files six tokens of שִׁית “set, put” here by spelling (Exo 33:4; 1Sa 4:20; Isa 22:7; Psa 3:7; 84:4; 140:6); they are not this verb.

stems.gloss: drink (water, wine, blood); eat and drink; drink a cup (of wrath); drink in (iniquity, scorn)

senses.definition: To take water or another liquid into the mouth and swallow it, for thirst and life: men and beasts at a well, a stream, a wadi or water out of the rock.

evidence.note: “Please let down your jar so that I may drink,” and she says, “Drink, and I will also water your camels.”
“You will strike the rock, and water will come from it, and the people will drink.”
Paul of the same water: “they all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from the spiritual rock … and the rock was Christ.”
Gideon's men at the water: those who lapped and those who knelt “to drink the water”.
God split the hollow at Lehi, water came out, “and he drank and his spirit returned, and he revived”.
The Egyptian “had not eaten bread and had not drunk water three days and three nights”; he ate and his spirit returned.
“You shall drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there.”
The Nile turned to blood: “the Egyptians were not able to drink water from the river.”
“If we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price.”
“Our water we drink for silver.”
David would not drink the water from Bethlehem's well: “the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives”.
The smith “does not drink water, and he tires”.
Of the land: it “drinks water of the rain of the heavens”.
“He will drink from the stream along the path; therefore he will lift up the head.”
The fat sheep drink the settled water and foul the rest with their feet; the flock drinks what they have fouled.
“Drink water from your own cistern”: keep to your own wife (Pro 5:18–20).

senses.gloss: drink wine or strong drink; drink to drunkenness
senses.definition: To drink wine or שֵׁכָר, often to drunkenness; and its refusal, by priests on duty, the Nazirite, the Rechabites and kings who must judge.

evidence.note: Noah “drank some of the wine and became drunk (וַיִּשְׁכָּר)”.
“They drank and became drunk with him.”
Elah “drinking himself drunk (שֹׁתֶה שִׁכּוֹר)” in Tirzah when Zimri struck.
Ben-hadad “drinking himself drunk in the huts”.
“Woe to the champions at drinking wine.”
“Drinking from bowls of wine … but not grieved over the breaking of Joseph.”
“Wine or strong drink do not drink, you or your sons, when you go into the tent of meeting, so you will not die.”
The Nazirite “shall not drink” vinegar of wine or any juice of grapes.
Of John: “wine and strong drink he will not drink” (οὐ μὴ πίῃ), the Nazirite's charge.
Hannah: “wine and strong drink I have not drunk, but I have poured out my soul before Yahweh.”
The Rechabites: “We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab our father commanded us.”
Not for kings to drink wine, “lest he drink and forget what is decreed and pervert the cause of the afflicted”.
Give it to the perishing: “he will drink and forget his poverty”.
Daniel asks for vegetables to eat “and water to drink” in place of the king's wine.
“The songs of the drinkers of strong drink.”
“Eat, friends; drink, and be drunk, beloved ones.”
“You drink, but not to drunkenness”: never enough.

senses.gloss: eat and drink: share a meal, feast; (negated) fast
senses.definition: With אָכַל: to eat a meal, alone or together, as covenant, feast or the plain enjoyment of life; and, denied, to fast or to refuse a host's table.

evidence.note: The elders of Israel on the mountain: “they saw God, and they ate and drank”: the covenant meal.
Isaac and Abimelech: “he made a feast (מִשְׁתֶּה) for them, and they ate and drank”, and swore an oath the next morning.
Under Solomon “Judah and Israel were many … eating and drinking and rejoicing”.
“They ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with great rejoicing,” and made Solomon king.
“Go, eat the fat and drink the sweet … for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.”
“Nothing better for man than that he should eat and drink and see good in his toil; this is from the hand of God.”
“Eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.”
Josiah “ate and drank and did justice and righteousness; then it was well with him”.
Before the calf: “the people sat down to eat and to drink and rose up to play”; quoted at 1Co 10:7.
Called to weeping, Jerusalem feasted: “Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”; quoted at 1Co 15:32.
“When you ate and when you drank, did you not eat and drink for yourselves?”
Job's sons made a feast and called their sisters “to eat and to drink with them”.
Uriah: “shall I go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife?”
Forty days and forty nights with Yahweh: “bread he did not eat and water he did not drink”; Deu 9:9, 18.
“Fast for me, neither eating nor drinking for three days.”
Nineveh's fast: man and beast “must not drink water”.
The man of God: “I would not eat bread and I would not drink water in this place”, as Yahweh commanded (1Ki 13:9, 16–22).
“The Son of man came eating and drinking (ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων)”, as John came neither eating nor drinking (Mat 11:18).
“That you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

senses.gloss: drink the wine of one's own vineyard
senses.definition: To plant a vineyard and drink its wine is to live settled in the land and enjoy one's labour; to plant and not drink is the curse of the covenant, and to plant and drink again is the promise of restoration.

evidence.note: “You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will not drink the wine.”
“You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.”
“I will restore the captivity of my people Israel … they will plant vineyards and drink their wine.”
Yahweh has sworn that strangers will not drink Israel's new wine: “its gatherers will drink it in the courts of my holiness”.
“My servants will drink, but you will thirst (תִּצְמָאוּ).”

senses.definition: To drink the cup from Yahweh's hand: to take the judgment he gives, until one staggers and falls. Said of Jerusalem, Edom and all the nations; and Jesus speaks of the cup his Father gave him to drink.

evidence.note: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and make all the nations drink it; they will drink and stagger … from the sword that I am sending.”
“Drink and be drunk and vomit and fall … Drinking you shall drink.”
“Those whose judgment was not to drink the cup will surely drink, and you will not be acquitted.”
“Jerusalem, who drank from the hand of Yahweh the cup of his heat … you drained it.”
“I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering … you will not drink it again.”
“A cup is in the hand of Yahweh … all the wicked of the earth will drink.”
“The cup of your sister you will drink … you will drink it and drain it.”
“As you drank on the mountain of my holiness, all the nations shall drink continually.”
“Drink, you also … the cup of Yahweh's right hand will come around to you.”
“From the wrath of the Almighty let him drink.”
The worshipper of the beast “will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, mixed undiluted in the cup of his anger”.
“Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?”; Mrk 10:38–39.
“My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done.”
“The cup that my Father gave me, shall I not drink it?”

senses.gloss: drink in, take in (iniquity, scorn, violence, poison); drink blood
senses.definition: Figurative: to take a thing in freely and constantly, as a man drinks water; and of beasts and birds, to drink the blood of the slain.

evidence.note: “A man drinking iniquity like water.”
Job “drinks scorn like water”.
The wicked “eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence”.
Sending words by a fool is “drinking violence”.
“The arrows of the Almighty are in me, whose poison my spirit drinks.”
Israel as a lion that “will not lie down until it eats prey and drinks the blood of the slain”.
Of Gog's host from the north, fallen on the mountains of Israel: the birds and beasts gathered to Yahweh's sacrifice “will eat flesh and drink blood … the blood of the princes of the earth”.
“Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?”
The Rabshakeh: men on the wall who will “drink their own urine with you”; 2Ki 18:27.

senses.definition: Passive: of a liquid, to be drunk.

evidence.note: “Any drink that is drunk (יִשָּׁתֶה) from any such vessel will become unclean.”

evidence.locator: Isa.22.13, שָׁתוֹת → πιεῖν, שָׁתוֹ → πίωμεν; Exo.32.6, שָׁתוֹ → πιεῖν; Jer.49.12, לִשְׁתּוֹת → πιεῖν, שָׁתוֹ → ἔπιον, תִּשְׁתֶּה → πίεσαι; πίνω renders שָׁתָה ×143

evidence.note: Isa 22:13 quoted: “Let us eat and drink (φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν), for tomorrow we die.”
Exo 32:6 quoted: “The people sat down to eat and to drink (πιεῖν).”
The cup Jesus is about to drink, after the cup of Jer 25 and 49.
“Drink from it, all of you … I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.”

parallels.note: Eat: “eat and drink” is the meal, the feast, and, denied, the fast.
Be drunk: what follows drinking wine to excess.

opposites.note: Thirst: Yahweh's servants drink, the rebels thirst.

phrases.gloss: eat and drink, for tomorrow we die

words.summary: The place-noun of the verb: the occasion of drinking, a feast, and in a few verses what is drunk. Forty-six times, nineteen of them in Esther.

senses.definition: A meal given by a host to guests, with wine: at a weaning, a wedding, a birthday, a covenant or a coronation, and the yearly days of Purim.

evidence.note: “Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.”
Laban's wedding feast for Jacob.
Samson's wedding feast, “for so the young men used to do”, seven days long (Jdg 14:12, 17).
Pharaoh's birthday feast for his servants.
Isaac's feast for Abimelech: “they ate and drank”.
Lot made the two men a feast and baked unleavened bread.
David's feast for Abner and his men.
Solomon's feast for his servants after the sacrifices at Jerusalem.
Nabal had “a feast in his house like the feast of a king … and he was very drunk”.
Ahasuerus's feast for the princes of Persia and Media; Est 1:5, 9; 2:18.
Esther's banquet for the king and Haman; Est 5:6 and 7:2 “the banquet of wine (מִשְׁתֵּה הַיַּיִן)”.
Purim: “days of feasting and rejoicing, and sending portions to one another and gifts to the needy”; Est 9:17–19.
When the days of the feast had gone round, Job offered for his sons.
“Harp and lyre and wine are at their feasts, but they do not regard the work of Yahweh.”
“Do not go into the house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.”
“Better to go to the house of mourning than the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men.”
“The good of heart has a continual feast.”
Babylon's feast: “I will make them drunk … and they will sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake.”
“Yahweh of Armies will make on this mountain for all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of wine on the lees”, and swallow up death for ever (Isa 25:8).

senses.definition: What is drunk: the king's wine, or drink given in payment.

evidence.note: The king's food “and the wine of his drinking (מִשְׁתָּיו)”; Dan 1:8, 16.
“The king, who has appointed your food and your drink.”
“Food and drink and oil” to the Sidonians and Tyrians for cedar from Lebanon.
Levi made Jesus “a great feast (δοχή)” in his house.
“When you make a feast (δοχή), invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.”
“The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast (γάμους) for his son.”
“Blessed are those called to the supper of the wedding feast of the Lamb.”

opposites.note: Mourning: the house of feasting set against the house of mourning.

words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic, five times, all at Belshazzar's feast. The perfect is written with a prothetic א (אִשְׁתִּיו, Dan 5:3–4), as in the Aramaic of the Targums.

senses.definition: To drink wine at a feast; at Belshazzar's, from the vessels taken from the house of God in Jerusalem, while praising gods of gold and silver.

evidence.note: “Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and drank wine before the thousand.”
The gold and silver vessels brought “that the king and his nobles … might drink from them”; “they drank wine and praised the gods of gold and silver”.
“You and your nobles … have drunk wine from them … but the God in whose hand is your breath you have not honoured.”
“The queen came into the banquet house (לְבֵית מִשְׁתְּיָא)”, the place of the feast of Dan 5:1.

words.summary: Once, Ecc 10:17. Its key also counts four tokens of the homograph שְׁתִי “warp” (Lev 13:49, 51, 53, 57), so lexicon-support shows five uses for one.

senses.definition: Drinking for its own sake, set against eating “for strength”.

evidence.note: Blessed the land whose princes “eat in due time, for strength and not for drinking (בַשְּׁתִי)”; set against Ecc 10:16, princes who feast in the morning.

senses.definition: The drinking at a feast, as it was ordered.

evidence.note: “The drinking (וְהַשְּׁתִיָּה) was by the law, none compelling”: each drank as he wished at Ahasuerus's feast.

words.summary: Nine times, all in Lev 13, always with עֵרֶב “woof” (in erev): “the warp or the woof” of linen or wool. Akkadian has both šatû “drink” and šatû “knot, weave” with šutû “warp”, and Arabic satan “warp” with no verb “drink”: the cognates show a second root šty “weave, set the warp” in the same letters, and no link to drinking is shown. Its key's tenth token, Ecc 10:17, is שְׁתִי “drinking”.

senses.definition: The threads set lengthwise on the loom, across which the woof is woven; named beside the woof as a part of a cloth that can carry a mark of disease.

evidence.note: The mark “in the warp or in the woof (בַשְּׁתִי אוֹ בָעֵרֶב) of linen or of wool, or in leather”.
“He shall burn the garment, or the warp or the woof.”
He shall tear it out “from the garment or from the leather or from the warp or from the woof”.
“The law of the mark of disease in a garment of wool or linen, or the warp or the woof.”

words.summary: Twice: Isa 20:4 and the plural שְׁתוֹתֵיהֶם (2Sa 10:4). Arabic ist (root s-t-h, plural ʾastāh) and Syriac ʾeštā “bottom, base” answer it; the Arabic root has a third radical h, not the y of “drink”, so the cognates point to another older root behind the same Hebrew letters, and no tie to drinking is shown. Its key also counts the name Seth (Gen 4:25; 5:3–8; Num 24:17; 1Ch 1:1) and Aramaic שֵׁת “six” (Ezr 6:15, in shesh), so lexicon-support shows eleven uses for two.

senses.definition: The seat of the body, uncovered to shame captives.

evidence.note: Hanun cut the garments of David's servants “in the middle, to their buttocks (שְׁתוֹתֵיהֶם)” and sent them away; they were “greatly ashamed” (2Sa 10:5).
Egypt's captives led away “naked and barefoot, and uncovered of buttock (וַחֲשׂוּפַי שֵׁת), the nakedness of Egypt”.

doctrine.statement: When Yahweh called Jerusalem to weeping and sackcloth, the city feasted instead: “Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die” (Isa 22:12–13). Paul takes up the same words: “If the dead do not rise, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die” (1Co 15:32). The Preacher says the same of life under the sun: eat and drink with joy, “for the dead know nothing … there is no work or knowledge or wisdom in the grave where you are going” (Ecc 9:5, 7, 10). From the verses: Paul sets the resurrection of the dead against eating and drinking for today, not a soul that lives on; if the dead are not raised, death ends the man and nothing is left to hope for. The hope he preaches is the putting on of immortality when death is swallowed up (1Co 15:54, quoting Isa 25:8).

The prophets promise that Israel, restored to its land, “will plant vineyards and drink their wine” (Amo 9:14), and that strangers will no more drink its new wine, “but its gatherers will drink it in the courts of my holiness” (Isa 62:8–9); “on this mountain” Yahweh will make for all peoples a feast of wine and swallow up death for ever (Isa 25:6–8). At the last supper Jesus said, “I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom” (Mat 26:29; Luk 22:18), and promised the twelve that they would “eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Luk 22:30). Those who drink the cup now “proclaim the Lord's death until he comes” (1Co 11:26). From the verses: the kingdom in which Jesus will drink again with his disciples is still to come, at his coming, on the earth where Israel's tribes are judged and vineyards are planted, and those who share his table must first be raised, since the death of Isa 25:8 is then swallowed up.

In the prophets the cup in Yahweh's hand is his judgment: Jeremiah makes the nations drink “the cup of the wine of wrath” until they stagger and fall before the sword (Jer 25:15–16, 27–28); Jerusalem drank “the cup of his heat” and Yahweh takes it from her hand (Isa 51:17, 22); “all the wicked of the earth will drink” (Psa 75:9). Jesus spoke of a cup he must drink (Mat 20:22), and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done” and “not as I will, but as you will” (Mat 26:39, 42); taken, he said, “The cup that my Father gave me, shall I not drink it?” (Jhn 18:11). From the verses: the Son had a will of his own and laid it down to the Father's, who gave him the cup to drink; it is the Father's to give and the Son's to receive. The same cup of wrath is still to be drunk by those who worship the beast (Rev 14:10).

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key שתה; no existing entry used it. BDB keys assigned: v.gi.aa verb, v.gi.ad מִשְׁתֶּה, v.gi.ab שְׁתִי “drinking”, v.gi.ac שְׁתִיָּה, v.gk.ab שְׁתִי “warp”, v.gj.ab שֵׁת “buttocks”, xv.bh.aa Aramaic verb, xv.bh.ab Aramaic מִשְׁתֵּה (Dan 5:10, root key משתה). Left unassigned: the zero-token cross-references m.dz.ab, xm.am.ag (מִשְׁתֶּה, “see שׁתה”), v.gh.am (שֵׁת, “see שׁתה”), xa.bi.ao (אִשְׁתִּיו, “see שְׁתָה”), and the empty root headings v.gj.aa, v.gk.aa. Shared tokens: v.gi.ab and v.gk.ab both count Lev 13:49, 51, 53, 57 and Ecc 10:17; only Ecc 10:17 is “drinking”. v.gj.ab counts the name Seth and Aramaic “six” (Ezr 6:15, already in shesh as xv.ah.ab); only 2Sa 10:4 and Isa 20:4 are “buttocks”. NO NAME FILE: Seth (Seth@Gen.4.25) is named from שִׁית “set, appoint” (Gen 4:25, שָׁת־לִי “God has appointed for me”), not this root, and שִׁית has no entry yet; give Seth a name file when it does. No other personal name is formed from שתה (Vashti is Persian). THREE ROOTS IN ONE SPELLING: “drink” (š-t-y in Akkadian, Ugaritic, Punic, Ge'ez, Aramaic, Syriac; Arabic has no verb šty “drink”, using šariba), “warp” (š-t-y “weave” in Akkadian beside šatû “drink”; Arabic satā/sadā), and “buttocks” (Arabic s-t-h, Syriac ʾeštā). All show š behind ש, so this is not a merged-letter split but homonyms in the same consonants; whether “warp” and “drink” were ever one root is open. A homograph split (entries for warp and buttocks apart) was considered and not made, following “one spelling, one entry”; review. Whether שֵׁת “buttocks, seat” rather belongs with שִׁית “set, sit” (seat as where one sits) is open; the Arabic h argues against both. Leads not followed: Akkadian šatû “drink” in CAD; Ugaritic šty in DULAT (not vendored); Punic šty in Krahmalkov; Payne Smith for ܐܫܬܐ “buttock” (SEDRA gives only “foundation”); Old Aramaic שׁתה. The Peshitta's own uses of ʾeštī and meštūtā (Mat 22:2; Jhn 2:1–2) are not yet added as syc words of the entry. Greek: brief lists no loans; πίνω, δοχή and γάμος are renderings only. Akkadian išdu “foundation” recorded as possible only. Wiktionary links Syriac ܫܬܐ to Arabic شَتَّى (šattā, “scatter”), not followed: no shared sense. The doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review; the Gog reference at Ezk 39:17–19 is noted in the drink-in sense.
